Welcome to St Paul's CofE Primary School
At St Paul's CofE Primary School, we believe that true education goes beyond the classroom walls. Our mission is to nurture the whole child, creating an environment where academic excellence meets personal growth. By fostering a foundation of love, faith, and hope, we empower our students to become compassionate leaders of tomorrow.
We are passionate about championing diversity and we are proud that our families come from all different cultures, beliefs, countries and family make-ups. Here, every child is celebrated for exactly who they are, and every family finds a place to belong.

Mission, Vision, Values and Ethos
The Fruit of the Spirit
St Paul's CofE Primary School is passionate about championing diversity and we are proud that our families come from all different cultures, beliefs, countries and family make-ups. We ensure contributions from different cultures are embedded in our curriculum.​
We believe that every child really does matter and we value each pupil as an individual. We encourage children to embrace our Christian values, based on the Fruit of the Spirit and follow our school behaviour code that embodies these, building mutual respect for all in our school.

St Paul's CofE Primary School, KH - Welcome from the Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to St Paul’s C of E Primary School - a place of warmth, aspiration and joyful learning where we are committed to providing education for life for every child and family in our community.
From the very beginning, in our award-winning Early Years, we nurture and support each child as they grow in confidence, independence and curiosity. Our children are known, valued and celebrated for who they are - and who they are becoming.
At St Paul’s, learning is rich and ambitious. Through exceptional experiences, we seek to inspire a love of learning and provide opportunities that build character, deepen spirituality and help children to thrive - academically, socially and emotionally. We develop every child’s voice and offer real leadership opportunities so they leave us confident, resilient and ready for the world.
Our curriculum reflects the diversity of our school community and is enriched through creativity, performance and the arts. Children explore big questions, enjoy cultural celebrations, take part in music, drama and sport - all while developing a deep sense of connection to themselves, each other and the wider world.
We are proud of our high standards and of the strong partnerships between children, staff, families, governors and our local church. Together we create a nurturing and inclusive environment, rooted in the Christian values of faith, hope and love, where wellbeing is prioritised and every child can flourish.
We are incredibly proud of our journey - from our ‘Excellent’ SIAMS to our ‘Good’ Ofsted and outstanding Early Years - but it is the smiles, the curiosity and the sense of belonging that truly define our school.
We would be privileged to be part of your child’s learning journey. Thank you for considering St Paul’s.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Paul's CofE Primary School, KH - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
At St Paul's we are educated for life with the love of God and Christian values at the heart of our school. The daily activity of Collective Worship is viewed as an integral and important part of the school day. The nine Fruits of the Spirit are often referred to, as is Jesus' teaching as shown through the Bible. We value the learning of other faiths and religions and celebrate what they offer in educating our pupils in our community. We are committed to respecting each other’s faith and culture, showing tolerance and understanding regardless of pupils’ beliefs.
Our collective worship is typically led by Mrs Stephenson, Miss Luker and Mr Rylett, the vicar at St Paul's Church. There are times when other members of staff and groups of pupils are involved or lead Collective Worship.
Collective Worship
Our programme of daily Collective Worship is central in sustaining and promoting our Christian foundation. Different elements of our Christian ethos and values are clearly planned for.
We take the themes of our collective worship from the traditions of the Christian values, British Values and our PSHE programme as well as events of the Christian calendar. Sometimes the themes of our collective worship reflect and build on topics that we teach as part of the school curriculum. We plan our collective worship as part of a series of themes well in advance of the day they take place
Our Vicar, Adam Rylett, leads Collective Worship on a weekly basis. Local, national and international events are drawn on to enhance our worship further and the importance of our Collective Worship themes. This is led by pupils who share their faith with the school community. Biblical teachings and stories are closely related to the school’s Christian values and to events in the world today.
We visit St Paul’s Church to celebrate Harvest, Christmas and Easter and the Leavers’ Service.
Prayer and reflection is also an important part of our school day.
Celebration Collective Worship
Every Friday, the whole school is invited to attend the Worship Celebration . Two children from each are class will be presented with a certificate for displaying aspects of the fruit of the spirit that week.
What have we been learning about in Collective Worship?
Harvest Festival
Our Harvest Service will be being held on Thursday 23rd October, in the school hall. Reception will celebrate Harvest at a different time.
All contributions will be donated via St Paul’s Church to support Kingston Foodbank and the Kingston Churches Action on Homelessness (KCAH).

pageCache.pageTitle: St Paul's CofE Primary School, KH - Global Neighbours
pageCache.text:
Global Community
At St. Paul's CofE Primary School, we're on a fantastic journey to become Christian Aid Global Neighbours, and it's all about making our world a better place.
Having achieved the Global Neighbours Award, we continue to weave global citizenship into the fabric of our school life. We empower our pupils to be courageous advocates, giving them the tools to speak out against injustice and take a stand on the issues that matter most. Central to this is our dedication to tackling prejudice the climate crisis; we recognise that stewardship of our planet is a shared responsibility. By understanding the link between environmental health and global equality, our students are learning to lead the way toward a more sustainable and just future for all.
Momentum Fundraising
Year 4 chose Momentum for their charity. Someone from Momentum came in to talk to use about what Momentum is and the work that they carry out. We held a pyjama day to remind us that many of the children who are not well wear pyjamas for a lot of the time. We had a film night to raise more money. We raised £262.40. Great work year 4!
Global Neighbours News!
Year 6 have been learning about flooding and how countries, who do not have the infrastructure that we do in the UK, can be left with devastating and long-term effects from this. The children have been looking at how they could design affordable and flood-resistant homes to beat the flood for these communities. We look forward to make these and testing them out after half term.
Courageous Advocacy- supporting, championing and speaking up for causes that are important and meaningful to them.
Fair Trade
In an exciting exploration of ethical eating and global citizenship, students embarked on a journey to discover the world of fair trade food.
The experience was not just about tasting delicious treats but also understanding the profound impact their choices can have on communities across the globe.
Practical Action
We're incredibly proud of our Year 6 students, who have been delved into a remarkable project focused on sustainable flood-resistant homes. Their dedication to learning, problem-solving, and making a positive impact was truly inspiring.
Students were learning about the unfortunate challenges faced by many countries affected by flooding and global poverty. Armed with their knowledge and guided by their compassionate hearts, they embarked on a mission to make a difference.
Designing Flood-Resistant Homes
Students have not only learned about the devastating effects of floods but have also rolled up their sleeves to create solutions. They have designed flood-resistant homes, specifically tailored to meet the needs of communities in dire need of resilient housing options.
In their project, our Year 6 students emphasized key aspects of flood-resistant home design, including:
Elevation: Elevating living areas to stay dry during floods.
Sustainable Materials: Using eco-friendly, flood-resistant building materials.
Raised Foundations: Preventing water from entering living spaces.
Flood Barriers: Incorporating flood barriers or gates to keep floodwaters at bay.
Rainwater Harvesting: Implementing systems to capture and use rainwater sustainably.
Energy Efficiency: Ensuring energy-efficient designs with renewable energy sources.
Community Involvement: Collaborating with local communities to meet their specific needs.
Education: Teaching residents about flood preparedness and sustainable living practices.
Disaster Resilience: Creating homes that can withstand various natural disasters.
Affordability: Ensuring the homes are accessible and affordable to those in need.
This project goes beyond the classroom. It instills a sense of social responsibility, environmental stewardship, and global citizenship in our Year 6 students. We're excited to see the positive impact their ideas and designs will have on communities facing the challenges of flooding and poverty.
We applaud our Year 6 students for their dedication to making the world a better place. This project showcases the power of education in empowering young minds to be future changemakers.

The Hive is operated by school staff and all children are familiar with the staff from working with them in school.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Paul's CofE Primary School, KH - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
At St Paul’s C of E Primary School, we firmly believe in the transformative power of music in education. We strive to create a vibrant musical environment where students are not only engaged and inspired but where music becomes an integral part of their daily experience. We place immense value on music's ability to enhance students' self-esteem, encourage creativity, build relationships, foster life skills, and enrich learning across the entire curriculum. We seek to instil in our pupils a profound awareness of their surroundings, acknowledging that music is a dynamic force that reflects culture and society rather than merely a subject on its own. By celebrating the joy of music, we aspire to create a school community where music is not only fun and for life but is truly for everyone, contributing to the holistic development of all our students.
How music is taught at St Paul’s
Music is taught at St Paul’s C of E Primary through the use of Sing Up (https://www.singup.org/). Sing Up Music provides primary schools with the foundation to deliver a creative programme of high-quality classroom music activity. It sets out the skills, knowledge, and understanding to be gained by all pupils at each stage of learning, including the Early Years Foundation Stage. Key stage 1 and Key stage 2 have an hour of music teaching a week and Reception are taught music for 30 minutes weekly.
In music lessons, children are actively involved in using and developing their singing voices, using body percussion and whole-body actions, and learning to play classroom instruments effectively to create and express their own and others’ music. Through a range of whole class, group and individual activities, children have opportunities to explore sounds, listen actively, compose and perform. Resources from Sing Up are used to ensure consistent musical development throughout the school. The children are introduced to a wide range of musical styles and genres from different times and places during music lessons. A wide variety of notations, including picture, graphic, rhythm and staff notation are integrated, wherever appropriate, with practical music-making activities.
What our children say about Music
‘At St Paul’s, you can write your own songs and become your own composer in Year 3.’
Year 6 - ‘We participate actively in our music lessons and learn engaging chants.’
‘Every term is different in Year 4, and we play instruments and listen to different songs.’
Aims
Foster a Love for Music: Cultivate a genuine appreciation and love for music, encouraging students to enjoy and engage with a variety of musical genres and styles.
Develop Musical Skills: Provide a foundation for the development of fundamental musical skills, including singing, playing instruments, listening, and rhythm.
Enhance Creativity: Stimulate and nurture creativity by giving students opportunities to compose, improvise, and express themselves musically.
Build Confidence: Empower pupils by building their confidence in musical expression, whether through solo performances, group collaborations, or other musical activities.
Encourage Active Listening: Develop active listening skills, enabling pupils to analyse and appreciate different musical elements, styles, and traditions.
Promote Cultural Understanding: Introduce students to a diverse range of musical cultures, helping them understand the cultural and historical contexts of various musical traditions.
Foster Collaboration: Encourage teamwork and collaboration through group music-making activities, ensemble performances, and shared musical experiences.
Instil a Lifelong Appreciation for Music: Aim to instil in students a lifelong appreciation for music, ensuring that they continue to engage with and enjoy music beyond their primary school years.
Promote Inclusivity: Create an inclusive music program that accommodates students with varying levels of musical aptitude, ensuring that all students feel welcome and capable of participating.
Encourage Reflection: Foster reflective practices, encouraging students to think critically about their musical experiences, assess their progress, and set goals for future development.
Our music intent - KS1:
To apply English and maths skills in music i.e. good speaking and listening skills when describing sounds or pieces of music, extending pupil’s vocabulary using musical terms, understanding the mathematics of the number of beats per bar and how this affects the feel of music.
For pupils to be resilient, able to persevere and learn from their mistakes when chanting, singing or playing instruments or body percussion.
To begin to foster a deep respect for beliefs, cultures, different world views and all that makes us unique by learning about music and musicians from different traditions.
For pupils to be able to problem solve in music, i.e. to experiment, create, select and combine sounds to give specific sound effects.
To be able to give their opinion about music that they have listened to.
To perform using their voices expressively and creatively and to play instruments musically.
For pupils to have a rich culture capital i.e. to appreciate and understand a range of live and recorded music.
To foster children who are appreciative of the range of music that is available to everyone to experience through listening to recordings, live performances and for the opportunities they have to learn to play different classroom percussion, as well as singing as a class and whole school.
Our music intent - KS2:
To apply English and maths skills in music i.e. good speaking and listening skills when analysing music, descriptive writing based on a piece of music listened to, using poems to inspire composition, extending pupil’s vocabulary using musical terms, understanding the mathematics of rhythmic notation.
For pupils to be resilient, able to persevere and learn from their mistakes when composing and performing, in order that they will sing and play instruments with increasing confidence and control.
To communicate effectively and confidently when expressing their opinions on music they have listened to, whether recorded or live, by professional musicians or their peers.
To foster a deep respect for beliefs, cultures, different world views and all that makes us unique by learning about music and musicians from different traditions.
For pupils to be able to problem solve in music, i.e. to choose appropriate sounds to give specific sound effects or represent feelings, atmospheres, places; to create a rhythm pattern that fits with given number of beats per bar; to match chords to accompany a melody.
For pupils to be able to use critical thinking skills when listening to music, to be able to give constructive feedback to others about their performances and compositions.
Pupils who serve, i.e. pupils who have individual instrumental lessons being willing to share their musical skills and knowledge in group work with other pupils who have not had as much experience as they have, such as singing worship songs in our church services.
Pupils who play and perform in solo and ensemble contexts, using their voices and playing musical instruments with increasing accuracy, fluency, control and expression.
For pupils to have a rich culture capital i.e. to appreciate and understand a wide range of music drawn from different traditions and from great composers and musicians; to develop a good understanding of the history of music.
To foster children who are appreciative of the vast range of music that is available to everyone to experience through listening to recordings, live performances and for the fantastic opportunities they have to learn to play different instruments such as the violin, ukulele and classroom percussion, as well as singing as a class, whole school or club.
What our children say about Music
‘Music at St Paul’s is really fun because we have the freedom of choice.’
Year 3 - ‘We try different instruments, which makes music at St. Paul's really fun.’

SUGAR SMART AND NUT FREE SCHOOL
We are a ‘Sugar Smart’ and nut free school. May we remind parents that sweets, including whole chocolate bars, are not permitted in school and should not be included in children’s lunchboxes. We have several children who are prone to anaphylaxis, please ensure that packed lunches do not contain nut products (including cereal bars, peanut butter and Nutella). Our school kitchen uses nut-free products.
Please remind your child that they are only permitted to eat pieces of fruit in the playground at break or lunchtime.
As we are a ‘Sugar Smart’ school, we ask that pupils do not bring in sweets or similar as birthday treats. As an alternative, parents can bring in fresh fruit for the class or donate a book or game to the class on their child's birthday.
Thank you for your support.

Isle of Wight
We have had a fantastic first day! Our adventure started with an exciting hovercraft trip from Portsmouth, and we arrived safely at Westbrook House full of energy and ready to explore.
The children have been having an absolute blast exploring the house and grounds. The games room has been a massive hit, and everyone was absolutely thrilled to discover two table tennis tables! We have already seen some great basketball matches and plenty of fun in the games area. Luckily, the weather has been quite kind to us, so we were able to spend lots of time playing outside and taking on the challenges of the low ropes course.
After working up a big appetite, dinner went down a treat tonight—a delicious, comforting meal of chicken, chips, and beans.
To wrap up a perfect first day, the brilliant Miss Simpson took to the stage as our official Quiz Master for a fun-filled general knowledge quiz. It was the perfect way to wind down after such an action-packed afternoon.
There are lots of tired eyes here now, so it is officially bedtime for us to rest up for another big day tomorrow. Goodnight from all of us at Westbrook House!
We have had another absolutely packed day here on the Isle of Wight! It was a rather rainy start to the morning after a very wet night, but we were pleased when the downpour began to ease up just in time for our walk down to the swimming pool. We enjoyed a lovely stroll along the seafront and were even treated to a few welcome rays of sunshine.
The pool was fantastic fun—we all got in together for a giant, high-energy splash about! Afterwards, we managed to eat our lunch on the beach and fit in a quick play in the sand before the heavens opened, leading to a very wet (but very giggly) walk back to the house. Some much-needed chill time and warm showers followed for everyone... or at least, that is what we teachers are hoping!
Once we were all dried off, the children threw themselves into the afternoon's entertainment. The house was buzzing with football, volleyball, giant chess, and plenty of competitive ping-pong.
A delicious dinner of spaghetti bolognese sorted everyone out and fueled us up for the absolute event of the year: the Westbrook House Disco! DJ Clark and MC Simpson completely rocked the decks, and the children partied incredibly hard. They've got some serious dance moves!
Be sure to check out the photo gallery to see all the action from today. We have a feeling everyone will sleep very well tonight!
We woke up to a much brighter start today, with a beautiful, sunny morning finally greeting us! We fueled up for the day with delicious pain au chocolat for breakfast before jumping on the coach and heading off to the famous Needles.
Our morning was packed with discovery. We watched a fascinating glass-blowing workshop and learned all about the incredible art of making glass shapes. Afterward, we explored the famous multi-coloured sands of the Isle of Wight and the children even got to make their very own sand souvenirs to show you when they get home. We also squeezed in a trip to the shop so everyone could pick out a few keepsakes and presents!
The weather kept things exciting for us—a few lucky groups managed to see the Needles perfectly before a sudden thick fog and what felt like gale-force winds rolled in! However, just two minutes after leaving the unique microclimate of the Needles on our way back to Westbrook House, the glorious sunshine was right back.
The rest of the afternoon was spent soaking up the sun back at the house, with the children tackling the low ropes, playing football, and enjoying the grounds.
After a delicious dinner of burgers, we headed outside for the perfect final evening activity: a traditional campfire with toasted s'mores. The wonderful Mrs. Stephenson led us all in a giant sing-along, which was the perfect way to cap off an amazing trip.
It is now time for our final night's sleep here at Westbrook House. We have had the best time, but we can't wait to see you all tomorrow!
We woke up early to glorious sunshine on our very last morning on the Isle of Wight! A hearty breakfast of sausages, hash browns, and beans set us up perfectly for a busy final morning. But before any activities began, we all joined in for an incredibly enthusiastic rendition of Happy Birthday for our special Isle of Wight Birthday Girl, Zara!
The children made the absolute most of their final hours in the beautiful grounds, enjoying games of giant chess, volleyball, and plenty of running around. They also tried their hand at a spot of archery, and some of the aim we saw was seriously impressive!
Afterwards, everyone packed up their final bits and pieces and we enjoyed lunch together in the sunshine—complete with birthday cake, of course!
We have now officially arrived back on the mainland and are safely on the coach making our way back to you. We have had the absolute best trip and made the most incredible memories together.
A special shout-out must go to our amazing Isle of Wight staff team, as none of this would have been possible without their hard work and energy. I have no doubt that they (and the children!) will sleep very well tonight.
See you all very soon!

Parent School Association
Thank You for all your support
Welcome to the St Paul’s Parent Staff Association (PSA) Every parent and carer at St Paul’s is already part of our Parent Staff Association — this is your community. Whether you have lots of time to give or just a little, your involvement makes a difference. We'd love to hear from you!
Parent School Association (PSA) – Supporting Our Primary School Community
The Parent School Association (PSA) is a voluntary organisation led by parents and carers, dedicated to raising essential funds for our primary school. Every parent, teacher, and carer is automatically a member, helping us build a thriving, supportive school community.
We welcome all contributions of time, skills, or donations, as every effort directly supports our fundraising activities and benefits the children. The money raised by the PSA is invested in vital school resources, learning materials, and equipment not covered by the standard school budget.
By supporting the PSA, you are helping to enrich the educational experience of every child, ensuring they have access to opportunities and resources that place them truly at the heart of our school.
The Aims of the Parent School Association (PSA)
The Parent School Association (PSA) plays a vital role in supporting our primary school. Our key aims are:
· To raise money for the school through creative and engaging fundraising activities.
· To build an inclusive and vibrant school community where parents, carers, teachers, and children feel connected and supported.
PSA Fundraising Events
The PSA organises a wide variety of fundraising events throughout the year, including:
· Summer and Christmas fairs
These events not only raise essential funds but also bring families together, strengthening our school community.
The PSA committee publishes a schedule of events on the school website, in the school newsletter, and across our social media channels – including the St Paul’s PSA Facebook page and Instagram account.
We also have a PSA WhatsApp group, where parents and carers can see upcoming volunteering opportunities and stay connected with the latest fundraising news. To join contact us at stpaulspsa@gmail.com.
There are many ways to support the PSA:
· Attend the next PSA meeting
· Volunteer with your class representative
· Join in at one of our fundraising events
· Share your own fundraising ideas – we’ll be happy to support and promote them
Every contribution, big or small, helps us provide resources and opportunities that directly benefit the children at St Paul’s Primary School.
PSA Committee and Class Reps
We are pleased to confirm our PSA Committee for this year as follows:
· PSA Chair: Becky (children in year 2 year 4)
PSA Class Reps 2025 – 2026
· Y1 – Emma, Holly, Kay and Thea
· Y2 – Steph and Ale
· Y4 – Julia, Louisa and Virginia
· Y5 – Caroline, Jo, Liz, Hannah, Fran and Kellie
· Y6 – Rachel, Emma and Hanna
Thank you to those who have volunteered as class reps for this school year. If you are would like to consider volunteering as a class rep, please email the PSA at stpaulspsa@gmail.com for more information.
Thank you for your support.
